subject: Human Evolution
title: The Shoe Problem
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Shoe Problem.

hook.text: We evolved to walk barefoot for millions of years. Shoes are only about 40,000 years old.

buildup.text: Modern cushioned shoes change our gait: heel-striking instead of the midfoot landing barefoot runners use.

discovery.text: Studies show barefoot runners have lower impact forces, reducing stress on knees and hips.

twist.text: But shoes protect against cuts, parasites, and rough terrain—essentials for urban life.

climax.text: The debate isn't shoes vs. no shoes—it's that our feet evolved for ground contact, not foam padding.

punchline.text: We padded the foot that evolution perfected.

quiz.question: How do modern shoes change our natural gait?
options: They encourage heel-striking instead of midfoot landing
